pii.definition: Any identifier that can link data to a specific person, such as a full name.
pii.protection: Remove or replace with synthetic names before sending to external AI services.

pii.definition: Personal or work email addresses are direct personal identifiers.
pii.protection: Anonymize or aggregate; blocklist personal domains.

pii.definition: Contact details that can be used for tracking or social engineering.
pii.protection: Redact unless the business task truly requires the number.

pii.definition: Home or work addresses reveal where a person lives and works.
pii.protection: Replace with city or region level data when the location matters.

pii.definition: Government-issued identifier, highly sensitive, often regulated.
pii.protection: Never send to an external service without specific legal basis.

pii.definition: Payment card data is regulated (PCI DSS) and valuable to attackers.
pii.protection: Mask to last four digits at most; use tokenization.

pii.definition: Financial account identifiers that enable fraud if stolen.
pii.protection: Redact fully; route through approved financial systems.

pii.definition: Internal identifiers that link activity to a customer record.
pii.protection: Synthesize or hash before external use.

pii.definition: Health conditions, medications, and lab results - protected by law.
pii.protection: Only approved clinical tooling may process health data.

pii.definition: Compensation data is confidential to the employee, manager, and HR.
pii.protection: Keep in approved HR systems; never share externally.

sensitive_personal_information: Criminal history and internal investigation data
secrets_detection: API keys and secret tokens used to authenticate to services
api_keys: Treat any key as live until proven otherwise
Detect common patterns: sk-, ghp_, AKIA, bearer tokens
Never log keys or paste them into chat tools
Use a secrets manager and rotate on any exposure

data_classification.label: Internal
data_classification.impact: Low to moderate impact if exposed

data_loss_prevention: Classify data at creation, not at the edge
Scan outbound channels for sensitive patterns
Block or warn before data leaves the boundary
Redact minimally so the task still works
Log and review every block or warning
privacy_principles: Least disclosure: send only what the task needs
Minimization: collect and share the smallest useful set
Purpose limitation: use data only for the stated task
Data protection by design and by default
The user owns the decision: humans approve external sharing
enterprise_ai_policies: No customer PII to public AI services
No credentials, secrets, or keys to public AI
No financial or medical records to public AI
No source code to public AI without approval
No confidential contracts to public AI
Approved internal AI tools with audit logging for sensitive data
prompt_hygiene: Strip identifiers before building a prompt
Use synthetic or aggregated data for examples
State in the prompt that data is de-identified
Never paste secrets to debug a tool
Review the final prompt for leftovers before sending
least_disclosure_principle: Share the minimum information that accomplishes the task
Ask: what does the model actually need to answer this?
A marketing email does not need card numbers or home addresses
Summaries and structure can usually be produced from synthetic data
